name: Neural (EEG)
signal_examples: EEG (scalp electrodes); fMRI (BOLD) as a lower-temporal-resolution, higher-spatial-resolution alternative
citation: Ienca, M., & Andorno, R. (2017). Towards new human rights in the age of neuroscience and neurotechnology. Life Sciences, Society and Policy, 13, 5. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40504-017-0050-1; Koelstra, S. et al. (2012). DEAP: A Database for Emotion Analysis using Physiological Signals. IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing, 3(1), 18-31. https://doi.org/10.1109/T-AFFC.2011.15
privacy_exit_point: Leaves the scalp as a weak electrical signal picked up by surface electrodes; can reveal cognitive or affective state well beyond what the wearer intended to disclose.
agency_control_point: The cap or headset can be removed at will, but there is no established way to know afterward what was inferred from a session, or to retract it.
notes: Illustrative ratings, not values these papers report directly. Gain reflects EEG's role as a direct, information-rich neural signal in multimodal affect studies (Koelstra et al.); privacy and agency costs reflect the 'mental privacy' and 'cognitive liberty' concerns raised specifically for neural data (Ienca & Andorno).

name: Autonomic (ECG/HRV)
signal_examples: ECG; heart-rate variability (HRV); also EDA/GSR as a related autonomic channel
citation: Koelstra, S. et al. (2012). DEAP: A Database for Emotion Analysis using Physiological Signals. IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing, 3(1), 18-31. https://doi.org/10.1109/T-AFFC.2011.15; Poria, S., Cambria, E., Bajpai, R., & Hussain, A. (2017). A review of affective computing: From unimodal analysis to multimodal fusion. Information Fusion, 37, 98-125. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.inffus.2017.02.003
privacy_exit_point: Leaves the chest (or wrist, for a photoplethysmography-based sensor) as an electrical or optical signal; the waveform itself is a biometric identifier, not just a heart-rate reading.
agency_control_point: A chest strap or wrist sensor can be removed at will; continuous background monitoring on a worn device can otherwise run without an ongoing prompt at each measurement.
notes: Illustrative ratings. Gain reflects DEAP's inclusion of peripheral autonomic channels alongside EEG for emotion recognition, and the multimodal-fusion survey's synthesis of when fusion improves on single-modality results; ECG is also itself a biometric identifier, which the privacy rating reflects.

name: Muscular (EMG)
signal_examples: Facial EMG (e.g. zygomaticus, trapezius); limb/prosthetic-control EMG
citation: Koelstra, S. et al. (2012). DEAP: A Database for Emotion Analysis using Physiological Signals. IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing, 3(1), 18-31. https://doi.org/10.1109/T-AFFC.2011.15
privacy_exit_point: Leaves the skin as a small electrical signal from the muscle beneath the electrode; localized to whichever muscle group is instrumented, unlike a systemic signal.
agency_control_point: Electrodes are physically attached and can be removed at will; each session requires deliberate placement, which limits collection without the wearer's direct involvement.
notes: Illustrative ratings. DEAP includes facial EMG among its peripheral physiological channels; gain here reflects its contribution to affect inference specifically, not to every possible inference task.

name: Behavioral (movement/speech)
citation: Onnela, J.-P., & Rauch, S. L. (2016). Harnessing smartphone-based digital phenotyping to enhance behavioral and mental health. Neuropsychopharmacology, 41(7), 1691-1696. https://doi.org/10.1038/npp.2016.7; Nautsch, A. et al. (2019). Preserving privacy in speaker and speech characterisation. Computer Speech & Language, 58, 441-480. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.csl.2019.06.001
privacy_exit_point: Movement leaves the body as accelerometer/gyroscope data from a worn device; speech leaves as audio that can be re-identified by voice alone, independent of what was said.
agency_control_point: A phone or wearable can be silenced or set aside, but passive background sensing is designed to continue without a prompt at each measurement.
notes: Illustrative ratings. Gain reflects digital-phenotyping evidence that passive behavioral sensing adds mental-health-relevant signal; privacy cost specifically reflects speech's voice-biometric re-identification risk (Nautsch et al.), separate from its content.

name: Subjective (self-report)
signal_examples: Momentary self-report of pain, mood, or symptoms
citation: Shiffman, S., Stone, A. A., & Hufford, M. R. (2008). Ecological momentary assessment. Annual Review of Clinical Psychology, 4, 1-32. https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.clinpsy.3.022806.091415
privacy_exit_point: Never leaves the body via a sensor at all - it exists only once the person chooses to disclose it, in their own words.
agency_control_point: The highest agency of any modality here: nothing is recorded unless the person actively responds, and they control what detail to include or omit.
notes: Illustrative ratings. Gain is capped below the biosignal modalities because self-report is lower temporal resolution and subject to recall/response bias (Shiffman et al.); agency cost is the lowest of the seven categories because the data is, by construction, the subject's own voluntary report rather than something inferred about them without their say.

name: Environmental (location/context)
signal_examples: GPS/location traces; ambient context (e.g. proximity, noise level)
citation: de Montjoye, Y.-A., Hidalgo, C. A., Verleysen, M., & Blondel, V. D. (2013). Unique in the crowd: The privacy bounds of human mobility. Scientific Reports, 3, 1376. https://doi.org/10.1038/srep01376; Dey, A. K. (2001). Understanding and using context. Personal and Ubiquitous Computing, 5(1), 4-7. https://doi.org/10.1007/s007790170019
privacy_exit_point: Never sensed from the body - it is ambient information about where the person is or what surrounds them, typically leaving via a phone's location service or nearby ambient sensors.
agency_control_point: Often collected passively in the background; many people are not shown each time a location point is captured, which limits their ability to authorize it in the moment.
notes: Illustrative ratings. Privacy cost is anchored to a specific, well-cited finding: four spatiotemporal points alone uniquely identify 95% of individuals in a mobility dataset (de Montjoye et al.). Gain reflects context-aware computing's general case that surrounding context improves interpretation of a primary signal (Dey).

name: Institutional (EHR/clinician)
signal_examples: Electronic health record entries; clinician notes or diagnoses
citation: Rothstein, M. A. (2010). Is deidentification sufficient to protect health privacy in research? American Journal of Bioethics, 10(9), 3-11. https://doi.org/10.1080/15265161.2010.494215
privacy_exit_point: Never sensed from the body directly - it already exists as a record in a clinician's or institution's system before this pipeline ever sees it.
agency_control_point: Typically the least agency of any modality here: entry, correction, and sharing of the record are usually mediated by clinicians or administrators, not decided directly by the person it describes.
notes: Illustrative ratings. Privacy cost reflects Rothstein's core finding that deidentified health data is more re-identifiable than commonly assumed. Agency cost is rated relatively high because institutional data is typically mediated by a clinician or record system rather than contributed directly by the person it describes.
